summary: SIEM feed c063_span_crc is degraded by 2 high-severity faults: 35.36% SPAN packet loss from oversubscription (1.55 Gbps into 1 Gbps) and 47,460 CRC/alignment errors on SIEM eth1. Combined, over one-third of traffic is lost before analysis and remaining frames are corrupted.

findings.root_cause: Physical layer fault on the link into SIEM eth1 (faulty cable/optic or duplex mismatch) causing 47,460 damaged frames with CRC/alignment errors (0.443% error rate vs 0.001% threshold).
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC discards corrupted frames; events and flows in those frames never reach detection engine, reducing coverage and causing incomplete/incorrect correlation.

recommended_fix.why: Clean L1 is required before any broker fix matters - replacing cable/optic, fixing duplex/speed and re-testing counters stops CRC drops so SIEM receives usable frames.

findings.root_cause: SPAN oversubscription at DIST-SW-02: Gi1/0/1 mirrors 16,575,000 packets (1.55 Gbps) but SPAN destination Gi1/0/48 is only 1 Gbps and discarded 5,860,680 packets on output (35.36% loss, sustained 100% load, bursts higher). SPAN destination cannot buffer oversubscription and tail-drops.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM misses 35%+ of packets/flows; attacks, C2 and lateral movement in dropped traffic are invisible, creating large blind spot despite SIEM being correctly configured.

recommended_fix.why: TAP does not drop under load like SPAN. Place passive TAP at Gi1/0/1 into packet broker, then filter/aggregate to fit SIEM 1 Gbps capacity or upgrade tool capacity/load-balance - eliminates SPAN-output discards and restores complete feed.
